### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>opencontainers/runc (github.com/opencontainers/runc)</summary>

### [`v1.5.3`](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases/tag/v1.5.3): runc v1.5.3 -- "Let me hear you make decisions without your television."

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/compare/v1.5.2...v1.5.3)

This is the third patch release in the 1.5.z release series of runc. It
includes a fix for a high-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-119101)
affecting users who checkpoint and restore containers, as well as a few
other fixes. Users are encouraged to update.

##### Security

This release includes a fix for the following high-severity security issue:

- [CVE-2026-119101][] allowed a malicious image, using crafted symlinks in
  its rootfs, to confuse the way runc names external mounts for CRIU, and so
  make `runc restore` bind-mount an arbitrary host directory into the restored
  container, read-write. Only users who both checkpoint and later restore
  containers running untrusted images are affected (checkpoint/restore
  requires root, so rootless runc is not affected). The same issue was found
  in crun ([CVE-2026-115520][]); CRIU itself is fixed in [CVE-2026-119614][].

  In addition, `runc restore` no longer makes read-only bind mounts writable,
  even temporarily, while preparing the container mounts.

[CVE-2026-119101]: https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/security/advisories/GHSA-g2c3-j8g3-7gpw

[CVE-2026-115520]: https://redirect.github.com/containers/crun/security/advisories/GHSA-2mxx-58qc-p466

[CVE-2026-119614]: https://redirect.github.com/checkpoint-restore/criu/security/advisories/GHSA-7ww7-53q2-wrwx

##### Fixed

- Running a container which does not have its own mount namespace no longer
  changes the propagation of host's `/` and of the parent mount of the
  container rootfs (they were made private or slave). ([#​5537](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5537), [#​5581](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5581))
- When making the container rootfs read-only (`root.readonly`), runc no longer
  clears the `nosuid`, `nodev`, `noexec` and `nosymfollow` flags of the rootfs
  mount (this only happened when not using a user namespace). ([#​5588](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5588), [#​5601](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5601))
- The `defaults` mount option is no longer passed to the kernel as
  filesystem-specific mount data, which made mounting filesystems that do not
  accept it (such as `tmpfs`) fail. ([#​5500](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5500), [#​5520](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5520), [#​5602](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5602))

##### Changed

- Updated github.com/moby/sys/capability to v0.5.0. ([#​5598](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5598), [#​5600](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5600))
- Various CI improvements. ([#​5481](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5481), [#​5482](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5482), [#​5488](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5488), [#​5574](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5574), [#​5586](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5586), [#​5590](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5590), [#​5609](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5609),
  [#​5615](https://redirect.github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5615))

##### Static Linking Notices

The `runc` binaries distributed with this release are *statically linked* with
the following [GNU LGPL-2.1][lgpl-2.1] licensed libraries, with `runc` acting
as a "work that uses the Library":

[lgpl-2.1]: https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/lgpl-2.1.en.html

- [libseccomp](https://redirect.github.com/seccomp/libseccomp)

Similarly, the `runc` binaries distributed with this release are also
*statically linked* with the following [MPLv2][mpl-2.0] licensed libraries,
with `runc` acting as a "Larger Work":

- [libpathrs](https://redirect.github.com/cyphar/libpathrs)

[mpl-2.0]: https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/MPL/2.0/

The versions of these libraries were not modified from their upstream versions,
but in order to comply with their corresponding licenses, we have attached the
complete source code for those libraries which (when combined with the attached
runc source code) may be used to exercise your rights under their respective
licenses.

However, we strongly suggest that you make use of your distribution's packages
or download them from the authoritative upstream sources, especially since
these libraries are related to the security of your containers.
